Yes. The current evidence (version 2, knowledge date 2026-11-12) shows that all four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day from 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-08. No thermal detections intersected the property in that period.

An earlier version (version 1, dated 2026-10-08) had a gap. The last day, October 7 to 8, was not yet covered because the near-real-time data hadn't been published. That version is superseded, and the gap has since been filled.

Two caveats:
- No detections does not prove that no fire occurred. Small, short, cool or cloud-obscured fires can be missed.
- The result says nothing about burned area, the cause of any change, or anything outside these dates.
